from_quote: The object of my last address to you was to engage your dispassionate consideration of the new Federal government
rationale: The paragraph refers to Cato's own "last address" and recalls its closing promise of observations "justified by reason and truth", which ends Cato 1.

from_quote: a writer under the signature of CAESAR, in Mr. Child's paper of the ist instant
rationale: The paragraph names "a writer under the signature of CAESAR, in Mr. Child's paper of the ist [1st] instant"; Caesar 1 appeared in the Daily Advertiser on Monday, October 1, 1787, and this essay is dated October 11, 1787.

from_quote: for Caesar himself declares that it is obviously the language of distrust
rationale: The paragraph repeats Caesar's words "obviously the language of distrust", attributing them to Caesar by name.

from_quote: his remarks on the questionable shape of my future
rationale: The paragraph takes up Caesar's "remarks" on Cato's "questionable shape", the phrase Caesar used of Cato's promised investigations.

from_quote: Caesar, with his usual dogmatism, enquires, if I had talents to throw light on the subject of legislation, why did I not offer them when the Convention was in session ? He is answered in a moment
rationale: The paragraph states Caesar's question, why Cato did not offer his talents while the Convention was in session, and sets out to answer it ("He is answered in a moment").
to_quote: If this demagogue had talents to throw light on the subject of legislation, why did he not offer them when the Convention was in session?

from_quote: if I had talents to throw light on the subject of legislation, why did I not offer them when the Convention was in session
rationale: The paragraph reproduces, as Caesar's enquiry, Caesar's question in nearly his own words, with "I" for "he".
to_quote: had talents to throw light on the subject of legislation, why did he not offer them when the Convention was in session

from_quote: But to call in dispute, at this time, and in the manner Caesar does, the right of free deliberation on this subject
rationale: The paragraph names Caesar's position that the plan must be taken as it is, without free deliberation, and sets out to refute it with a history of the Convention's appointment.
to_quote: just take it as it is and be thankful
